title: Research: pool PR #2269's 76 private T74 cleanup buffers into a 48-field bank
head: caba809dc9770a21f3b584ce9f3c8433a5768e83
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

PR2269's borrowed T74 words allocate 76 private cleanup buffers. This package gives a source-pinned static allocation using **44 fields forward and 48 in the inverse-transpose orientation**, so one common 48-field bank saves **28 fields**. It adds no arithmetic: 151/409 exact zero operations are omitted and all remaining operations retain their order. All 661 ordinary cleanup-entry arrays are arbitrary, and every pool field returns to zero.

The result is a **finite allocation construction and scoped proof**, packaged at `research/t74-cleanup-buffer-pooling/` (this PR). The two enclosing source words have the same literal cleanup list; both source bindings and both orientations are checked.

Interval coloring plus simultaneous-live witnesses proves 44/48 optimal in the declared zero-to-zero interval-allocation class. A stronger dual witness gives 48 distinct nonzero literal values at event 2686; its rows contain no remaining warp symbols, so it proves the common 48-field capacity sharp for direct literal storage even with equal-value coalescing. This excludes encoding, address packing, ordinary-register borrowing, spills, recomputation, reordering and new cleanup circuits. At the first forward peak there are two equal-value pairs; no broader forward-only minimum is claimed.

No supplier adoption, κ change, recursive-profile improvement, full-record verification or selected-frontier change is claimed. Native allocation/routing/CLEAR accounting, native lowering and phase bindings, precision/tape, whole-call admission and later 78-buffer words remain unchecked. The README gives the exact proof and boundary of the result.

## Validation

Python **3.12.3**, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/t74-cleanup-buffer-pooling
python3 -I -O -B research/t74-cleanup-buffer-pooling/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/t74-cleanup-buffer-pooling/check_dense.py
```

Registered replay and metadata/source pins pass. The exact engine derives all nonzero intervals, checks each allocation/release at zero, replays the static pool, and compares all ordinary output coefficients. The stored receipt contains every plan/interval/omission and a 48-distinct-value dual witness using signed 16-bit inputs. No predecessor Python code is imported or executed.

Six controls per bound case reject overlapping allocation, early release, dirty pool entry, a wrong-sign closing ADD, an unallocated zero read, and an inverse-warp sign change that changes the ordinary map. The separate dense interpreter checks two noncommuting 2-by-2 specializations over each of primes 65537 and 1000003, all **1322 scalar input columns** per case, every lifetime, peak rows, the full pool boundary and scratch restoration: eight cases. This supports the exact rational/free-algebra proof; finite-field checks alone are not presented as that proof.

Git-free read-only relocated optimized replays pass. Source-byte corruption, integer-to-Boolean receipt corruption and attempted output overwrite reject. Replays leave package bytes unchanged. `git diff --check` and package metadata/pin checks pass. Full native/global/outer cold replay, later-word transfer, proof-assistant checking, hosted CI and independent human review were not run or claimed.

## Open next questions

1. Emit the static allocation in the native cleanup, then check routing, CLEARs and full physical stock. The logical certificate does not discharge those charges.
2. Pin a later 78-buffer word and recompute its lifetimes; do not inherit the number 48 by lineage.
3. Test forward-only equal-value coalescing of `(1015,1202)` and `(1031,1214)` against their later writes. Agreement at one cut does not justify merging lifetimes; the dual direct-storage floor remains 48.

The README and TASK.json give first steps and blockers.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

Separating private-zero cleanup from the changing record made a bounded, reusable check possible. Publishing a stable cleanup-event interface and a separate physical-stock invoice with future borrowed-word records would make lifetime and allocation audits easier to compare.
